title: Prefetch window hit-rate decomposition: cost impact workbook (Q3 2026) - working
content:
Working version - do not finalize

Purpose:
This worksheet decomposes observed hit-rate gains from an adaptive prefetch window (client-side + runtime prefetch) across request size strata and estimates downstream cost impact at scale. Goal is to produce an actionable recommendation (alpha rollout knobs) and a measurement plan for the next 2-week experiment.

Executive summary (top-line):
- Baseline: no prefetch, KV prefix cache only (current prod sample): overall prefix hit = 14%, KV-hit-for-remaining = 6%. Baseline token spend per 1M requests = 450M gen-tokens (model tokens) * $0.00045/token = $202,500.
- Aggressive prefetch (window = 1.5k tokens): measured +prefetch overhead of 8% extra token work on misses, but net prefix hit increases to 36% and KV effective hit to 18%. Modeled cost reduction = ~21% (net).
- Conservative prefetch (window = 512 tokens): modest overhead (2.2%) with hit improvements to 22% prefix / 10% KV; modeled cost reduction = ~9% (net).
- Recommendation: run a canary for conservative prefetch first (512 tokens window) on 5% traffic, instrument token-level deltas and latency p95. If stable, ramp to 25% and evaluate aggressive mode on high-affinity request bucket only.

Key assumptions (editable cells):
1) Token price for generation: $0.00045 per generated token (hosted mixed GPU pool).
2) Cost for KV read (per request cost equivalent): modeled as $0.00002 per request (to approximate memory/CPU + network).
3) Average request distribution by output token length: see distribution table below.
4) Prefetch overhead only occurs on cache misses (we pre-generate tokens that might not be used).
5) Cold-start prefix hit excluded (only steady-state traffic modeled).

Tables (spreadsheet view, rows = request-length buckets):
Columns: bucket_label | pct_requests | avg_output_tokens | baseline_prefix_hit | baseline_kv_hit | pref_window | pref_overhead_pct | new_prefix_hit | new_kv_hit | est_tokens_saved_per_req | est_tokens_extra_prefetched_per_req | net_tokens_delta_per_req | pct_cost_reduction | notes

1) tiny (<=16 tokens) | 24% | 10 | 8% | 2% | 512 | 1.1% | 18% | 4% | 1.6 | 0.11 | +1.49 | 6.1% | small wins but low absolute token volume
2) short (17-64) | 38% | 34 | 12% | 5% | 512 | 2.4% | 24% | 9% | 6.1 | 0.8 | +5.3 | 8.7% | majority of requests, good ROI
3) med (65-256) | 22% | 112 | 14% | 7% | 512 | 3.6% | 28% | 11% | 22.4 | 4.0 | +18.4 | 10.9% | highest absolute token savings
4) long (257-1024) | 12% | 420 | 16% | 10% | 512 | 4.8% | 30% | 14% | 97.2 | 18.0 | +79.2 | 14.6% | bursty but large per-req effect
5) xlong (>1024) | 4% | 2200 | 10% | 8% | 512 | 6.5% | 20% | 12% | 308.0 | 142.0 | +166.0 | 7.2% | high overhead; treat conservatively

Notes on the table: net_tokens_delta_per_req is positive when tokens saved > tokens prefetched (= net reduction). pct_cost_reduction computed against baseline token spend for that bucket with model token price and KV-read modeling applied.

Sensitivity runs included (tabs):
- price-sensitivity: token price +/- 25% changes ROI by roughly +/- 5–6 percentage points.
- hit-elasticity: if new_prefix_hit is 5 percentage points lower than modeled, net savings drop by ~40% in med/long buckets.
- client-variation: mobile clients have 12% lower observed hit due to truncated prompts; consider server-side prefetch only for mobile.

Operational tradeoffs and risk register:
- Increased server-side compute due to prefetch on misses (memory pressure for KV + transient L2 cache pressure). Mitigation: cap prefetch CPU concurrency per pod, require dynamic shedding if OOMs approach threshold.
- Amplified regret on hallucinating prefetch content for non-deterministic completions. Mitigation: limit prefetch to deterministic tokens (e.g., completion tokens that are continuation of strong prefix signals).
- Observability gaps: need token-level telemetry (already scaffolded in PR #418) and per-route prefetch counters.

Measurement plan (2-week experiment):
- Week 0: roll conservative prefetch (512) to 2% traffic, collect 48h of token-level traces, measure p50/p95 latencies, CPU/memory, cache occupancy.
- Week 1: expand to 5% if no adverse signals. Run A/B with no-prefetch, instrument delta in tokens per request and request-level cost.
- Week 2: cohort analysis by client platform, request path, and hour-of-day. Decide on ramp to 25% and/or target-only aggressive prefetch for long-request buckets.

Deployment knobs for rollout (config keys to expose):
- prefetch.window_tokens (int)
- prefetch.max_concurrency_per_pod (int)
- prefetch.client_allowlist (list)
- prefetch.sampling_rate (float)
- prefetch.determinism_threshold (float) // avoid prefetch for low-confidence continuations

Action items (owner and ETA):
- Instrumentation: Marco Ruiz to land token-level counters + per-route tag (JIRA-11234) by 2026-07-20.
- Canary config: Lina Chen to produce helm patch with knobs and default conservative values by 2026-07-24.
- Risk runbook: Tomás Alvarez to draft OOM and CPU shedding runbook by 2026-07-28.
- Experiment analysis notebook: Aisha Patel will produce final cost/profitability matrix and recommend roll/no-roll decision by 2026-08-09.

Unresolved questions (to discuss with serving-runtime):
- Should prefetch be implemented as synchronous post-cache-read call or delegated to background worker? Latency vs. complexity tradeoffs.
- Is the KV store instrumentation granular enough to attribute per-prefetch read costs?

Appendix: calculation snippets (copy-paste into cell):
- net_tokens_saved_per_bucket = requests_per_bucket * (new_prefix_hit - baseline_prefix_hit) * avg_output_tokens + requests_per_bucket * (new_kv_hit - baseline_kv_hit) * avg_output_tokens
- gross_model_cost_reduction = net_tokens_saved_total * token_price
- prefetch_added_cost = total_requests_prefetched * avg_prefetch_extra_tokens * token_price + total_prefetch_reads * kv_read_cost
- net_savings = gross_model_cost_reduction - prefetch_added_cost

End of working sheet. Keep this doc as the single source for the experiment; if you fork, please append _fork in the filename.
